verdict: v3 FAILED. Both stages trained to completion and neither produces intelligible Nepali. v2 (milanakdj/pocket-tts-nepali-6l) remains the shipping model.

eval_set.protocol: held-out target utterance; voice prompt is a different clip of the same speaker identity taken from the train split. Verified: all 100 targets are in valid_v3 and none appear in train_v3, so these numbers are directly comparable with the published v2 table.

teacher_24l_v3.guidance: none (the pocket-tts inference path has no cfg_coef; this teacher was trained to be sampled at sample_cfg_coef 2.0, so this is its weakest mode)

inference_settings.note: the v3 thresholds were chosen on 40 calibration utterances disjoint from this eval set; at the -4.0 default the v3 student emits 0.26x the reference duration

calibration_set_40_utts_disjoint.purpose: choose eos_threshold/temperature without touching the eval set, and carry a real-human ceiling plus a v2 control so the v3 CER is readable

v3_teacher_guided_best.note: 6-8 of 40 utterances returned an empty generation

training_objective.note: the run's own loss said it failed; v3 at step 200000 is worse than v2 at step 5000

notes: real_human rows are the ceiling: the genuine recording of the same utterance scored through the identical pipeline, not a competitor. Absolute values are not comparable across the two ASR rows. The v2 rows here reproduce the published v2 table exactly, which is the check that the harness is unchanged.
